text: An annotation is declared and read reflectively but nothing is ever found. What is the most likely cause?
choices: `@Target` was omitted, so the compiler discarded it as unplaceable.
Its retention is not `RUNTIME`, so it did not survive into the loaded class.
The annotated members are private, and annotations are only readable on public ones.
It lacks a member named `value`, which reflection requires in order to match.
explanation: The default retention is `CLASS` — kept in the class file but not loaded — which is almost never what anyone wants. An annotation intended for reflection must be `RUNTIME`. It is the commonest annotation bug precisely because everything compiles and there is no error to read; the code simply finds nothing.
